extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting short humor/comedy pieces to McSweeney’s Internet Tendency
extracted.subtask_description: Submission guidelines for short-form humor/comedy pieces (lists, open letters, monologues, etc.) to McSweeney’s Internet Tendency, including procedural rules, formatting, content preferences, and eligibility. Focused on how to prepare and send pieces for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission inboxes / routing
rubrics_metrics.description: General website submissions should be sent to [email protected]. Lists, open letters, timely pieces, and New Food Reviews have their own specific inboxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submissions: [email protected]; Lists submissions: [email protected]; Open Letters: [email protected]; Reviews of New Food: [email protected]. Use the relevant inbox for the type of piece you are sending — the staff will route internally if needed, so pick one if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submissions (requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely submissions are for super topical pieces that HAS to run in the next day or else risk losing relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark the subject field in your email as “TIMELY.” Explain why the piece is super timely and feel free to include a link to a reputable news site for proof. Note: submissions sent on Friday afternoons (EST) or over the weekend will be replied to the following Monday (on Tuesday after three-day weekends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send to multiple submission addresses simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: Sending the same submission to multiple McSweeney’s inboxes at once is unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions go to the same editor anyway; if you’re unsure which email to use, pick one. This rule also applies to lists submissions (previously allowed up to three lists at a time; now strictly enforced one at a time).

rubrics_metrics.name: No AI-assisted writing
rubrics_metrics.description: McSweeney’s accepts no writing aided in any manner by AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before publishing any writing—from a letter to a book-length work—authors published at McSweeney’s will be asked to attest that AI played no part in the creation or writing of that work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitches discouraged; submit completed drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don’t send pitches. Submit only completed drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches are unnecessary; the editors want finished pieces rather than proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length limits and preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be shortish with an absolute maximum of 1,200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They veer toward pieces under 1,000 words and favor even shorter pieces. (Historical joke: submissions of exactly 742 used to automatically appear on the site.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Author credit and contact format
rubrics_metrics.description: Your name should be on your submission. Put it under the title of your piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions must look like: My Funny Experience [story title]* By William Williams [author’s name] [email protected] [email address] @wilywill [social handles (preferred but not required)]. The email listed should be the one you want linked to your byline; if you don't want it linked, tell them. Submissions must be credited to a person with a first and last name (pseudonyms are discouraged).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line should contain some indicator of what is contained in your submission — a version of the title is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use clickbaity or all-caps subject lines such as YOU’RE GOING TO LOVE THIS, INCREASE INCHES AND ENERGY TODAY, or INVITATION TO LINKEDIN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letters: optional and short
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letters are unnecessary but not forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you include one, keep it very short — longer than three and a half sentences there’s a fair chance it won’t be read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paste content into email; no attachments or links
rubrics_metrics.description: Please paste the entire document into the email message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share Google docs or links to private blogs. Do not send attachments — the editors state: 'We are afraid of what these attachments may be carrying.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit one thing at a time
rubrics_metrics.description: You should only have one active submission with McSweeney’s at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you receive a response about your current submission, feel free to send another. This rule now also includes lists submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not format your piece in an unusual way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use colors or fun fonts. Don’t describe how your piece would be best formatted because the site probably cannot achieve special formatting. Avoid clever formatting that renders the piece illegible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title importance and style
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of your submission is important and should quickly lure readers in and reveal the premise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid generic titles like 'A Phone Call' or 'Rabbits' in favor of funny, eye-catching titles that cleverly reveal premise (examples given). Do not title pieces in all-caps. Do not make the joke of titling your piece 'My Funny Experience' (overused). Titles should make readers think 'This is funny and seems worthy of the five minutes of free time I have.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously published material ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously published work cannot be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes content that has appeared on blogs, tumblrs, or sandwich boards. Do not send links to such previously published material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment policy summary
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be payment for accepted general, open letter, and lists submissions when Patreon funding goals are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment will be modest. Currently they cannot pay for New Food Reviews; they hope to pay more as Patreon support grows. The site has historically not been monetized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights retained by author; site archiving
rubrics_metrics.description: You retain rights to your work after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published work will be housed in McSweeney’s internet archives in perpetuity, and the site may re-post a link to your piece on social media from time to time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Average response time is 7.39 days, with longer waits possible for lists, open letters, and new food submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses may be shorter and vaguer than desired due to small editorial staff. Expect delays for weekend submissions (see timely note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible reasons for nonresponse
rubrics_metrics.description: Common logistical reasons you might not hear back include spam-blocking, accidental deletion, or recipient-side spam filtering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: 'Our spam-blocking software thought you were concerned about the size of our genitals.' 'We (accidentally) deleted your submission without responding.' 'You have an overaggressive spam-blocking program that rejects our reply.'

rubrics_metrics.name: If you don’t hear back: recommended action
rubrics_metrics.description: If you haven’t heard within the stated time frame, resend your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resending takes less time to respond to than answering a query. (Humorous suggestion: rail to your friends about the callous insensitivity of free web outlets, but the actionable guidance is to resend.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Features that reduce likelihood of acceptance (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of submission types, content features, and formatting choices that 'do not help one’s cause' and may reduce acceptance chances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: poetry; book reviews; short stories; personal essays; submissions sent to several publications/undisclosed recipients; formatted like a news article; over the word limit; includes the words 'these days' or 'nowadays'; did not take place in a jungle (joke); contains more than 1.79 ironic exclamation points; did not capitalize the first letters of sentences; not credited to a person with a first and last name; credited to an obvious pseudonym; included clever formatting rendering it illegible; subject matter similar to something recently published on the site; a list of goofy email names from spam or funny texts from a friend; submissions about being rejected by a humor website; bucket list featuring different types of actual buckets; Christmas-themed in May; riffs/sequels to McSweeney’s pieces you did not write; submission mentioning 'McSweeney’s' in title/text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific caution about New Food Reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews of New Food have a dedicated inbox and currently cannot be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send New Food Reviews to [email protected]. The site hopes to pay for New Food Reviews in the future if Patreon funding increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for additional questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional questions are answered via a specific editorial address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email submission-related questions to [email protected].
